requirements.title: The /graph page shall provide a persistent control for switching between force-directed and swim-lane rendering modes

amended.reason: Originally specified as a directly-visible toggle. The shipped design instead uses a persistent "Options & help" button (always visible) that opens a panel containing the layout-mode toggle. This was an explicit, live product decision made during epic scQi8pt, not a silent implementation drift.

vision.paraphrase: The graph view provides two selectable layout modes accessible via a persistent control to let users switch between force-directed and swim-lane presentations.
The mode toggle is reachable via a prominent, persistent control on the interface that enables switching between the two layout presentations.

conops.paraphrase: When a visitor opens the persistent options control and activates the layout-mode toggle, the interface responds by switching the board rendering between force-directed and swim-lane modes.

requirements.title: The /graph page shall switch between layout modes without making a new network request for graph-data.json or vector-index.json

vision.paraphrase: Switching between modes is an instant client-side operation with no data refetch, allowing both modes to share the same fetched assets.

conops.paraphrase: When the visitor toggles the layout mode, the board re-renders instantly using the already-fetched data without triggering new network requests.

requirements.title: The /graph page shall re-fit the force-directed camera to the graph bounds when a visitor toggles from swim-lane mode back to force-directed mode

amended.reason: The requirement was inverted: issue #4 finding A2 showed that restoring a stale pan/zoom left the visitor staring at a tiny off-screen clump. ConOps S7.9 now requires camera re-fit on switch. The prior pan/zoom state is deliberately discarded.

vision.paraphrase: Camera re-fit on layout switch (not pan/zoom restoration) fixes issue #4 finding A2, ensuring the visitor never faces an off-screen clump after toggling modes.

conops.paraphrase: When a visitor toggles back to force-directed mode, the camera re-fits to show all nodes in the viewport; the prior pan/zoom state is discarded to ensure readability.

requirements.title: The /graph page shall render nodes in swim-lane mode grouped into horizontal lanes by folder/taxonomy value, with at most 4 lanes visible

vision.paraphrase: Swim-lane mode organizes nodes into up to 4 horizontal lanes grouped by their folder/taxonomy classification, with the largest folders each receiving their own lane.

conops.paraphrase: When the visitor toggles to swim-lane mode, the board re-renders with nodes organized into horizontal lanes, each grouped by its folder/taxonomy value, capped at 4 visible lanes.

requirements.title: The /graph page shall collapse folder/taxonomy values beyond the 4 largest into a single shared "Other" lane in swim-lane mode

vision.paraphrase: Folders beyond the 4 largest (measured by node count) collapse together into a single shared 'Other' lane to maintain the hard 4-lane visual constraint.
The 4-lane cap is a hard visual constraint enforced by collapsing all folders beyond the 4 most-populated into a shared 'Other' lane.

conops.paraphrase: When the swim-lane board renders, folders beyond the 4 largest are grouped together into a single lane, preserving the fixed 4-lane layout.

requirements.title: The /graph page shall render each node in swim-lane mode as a labeled pill shape displaying the node's title

vision.paraphrase: Swim-lane mode renders nodes as labeled pill-shaped elements (rather than bare dots), each displaying the page's title inline.

conops.paraphrase: When the swim-lane board renders, nodes appear as pill-shaped elements with inline title text, arranged within their respective lanes.

requirements.title: The /graph page shall display all swim-lane mode lanes within the viewport without a vertical scrollbar at default viewport size

vision.paraphrase: The 4-lane cap enforces a hard visual constraint requiring all lanes to fit within the viewport without vertical scrolling at default size.

conops.paraphrase: When the swim-lane board renders, all lanes fit within the visible viewport without requiring vertical scroll, maintaining full visibility of the layout.

requirements.title: The /graph page shall NOT pan or zoom the camera view when a visitor clicks a node in swim-lane mode

vision.paraphrase: Swim-lane mode uses a static, fixed-position board layout without camera pan/zoom, distinguishing it from force-directed mode's click-to-center behavior.

conops.paraphrase: When the visitor clicks a pill node in swim-lane mode, the board position remains unchanged, maintaining the static layout perspective.

requirements.title: The /graph page shall hide edges by default in swim-lane mode until a node is clicked

vision.paraphrase: Swim-lane mode hides connector edges by default, revealing them only when a node is clicked to animate the connection visualization.

conops.paraphrase: When the swim-lane board renders, no connector lines are initially visible, keeping the lanes clean until the visitor interacts with a node.

requirements.title: The /graph page shall animate a curved connector line from a clicked node to each of its related nodes, drawing smoothly from source to destination over approximately 950 milliseconds

vision.paraphrase: Swim-lane mode uses animated curved connector lines drawn from a clicked node to each related node, directly mirroring the Nate Herk 'AI Stack, Connected' reference demo.

conops.paraphrase: When the visitor clicks a pill node, curved connector lines animate smoothly from that node to each related node across the lanes.

requirements.title: The /graph page shall clear previously animated connector lines and draw new ones when a different node is clicked in swim-lane mode

conops.paraphrase: When the visitor clicks a different node, the prior connector lines immediately clear and new lines animate from the newly clicked node.

requirements.title: The /graph page shall open a side panel displaying the clicked node's page detail and a "View source on GitHub" link when a node is clicked in swim-lane mode

vision.paraphrase: Swim-lane mode integrates the same side-panel behavior as force-directed mode, opening to display page detail and GitHub source links on node click.
The side panel slides in without full page navigation, maintaining graph context visibility and providing consistent access to page detail across both layout modes.

conops.paraphrase: When the visitor clicks a pill node, the side panel opens to show the node's page detail including title, tags, and status dot, plus a GitHub source link.

requirements.title: The /graph page shall remain interactive (clickable) in swim-lane mode when rendering a graph of at least 40 nodes

vision.paraphrase: The seed/demo public vault is seeded with 40+ sourced references on AI adoption in enterprises, representing the expected data scale the feature must handle reliably.

requirements.title: The /graph page shall render swim-lane mode correctly with an empty graph (zero nodes), displaying an empty-state message instead of a blank canvas

vision.paraphrase: Swim-lane mode is a peer rendering mode to force-directed mode over the same graph-data.json; it inherits the same robustness bar for the zero-node case that force-directed mode already commits to, so it must not present a broken or blank board when the vault has no content.

conops.paraphrase: PM-derived edge case: swim-lane mode is a new rendering path independent of force-directed mode's canvas code, so it can fail differently on the same zero-node input; parallels the existing force-directed empty-state requirement (TOR-02-mqgZkBc) to keep the two modes' failure behavior consistent.

requirements.title: The /graph page shall hide zero-degree nodes from the swim-lane board by default

captured_retroactively.reason: Implemented and live-tested against the real second-brain vault during the epic's UX redesign before it had formal TOR coverage; captured now as part of requirements reconciliation.

vision.paraphrase: A large, sparsely-connected vault should still fit legibly within the fixed 4-lane, no-scrollbar swim-lane board; nodes with no connections at all add visual noise without navigational value.

requirements.title: The /graph page shall reveal low-connectivity nodes in swim-lane mode when a connected node is clicked, rendered with a dashed style

captured_retroactively.reason: Implemented and live-tested against the real second-brain vault during the epic's UX redesign before it had formal TOR coverage; captured now as part of requirements reconciliation.

vision.paraphrase: Peripheral, low-connectivity pages should still be reachable through the graph's click-to-reveal interaction rather than being permanently invisible, distinguished visually (dashed styling) from always-visible nodes.

requirements.title: The /graph page shall display a "+N more" affordance in each swim-lane whose hidden low-connectivity nodes number at least one, reporting the exact count hidden from that lane

vision.paraphrase: Hidden-node transparency surfaces zero/low-degree nodes via a '+N more' affordance instead of silently dropping them, fixing issue #4 finding A7.

conops.paraphrase: When a lane has hidden low-connectivity nodes, the board displays a '+N more' affordance showing exactly how many nodes are hidden, preventing silent omission.

requirements.title: The /graph page shall render every hidden low-connectivity node of a lane onto the board when a visitor activates that lane's "+N more" affordance

vision.paraphrase: The '+N more' affordance is not merely a count but an interactive control that reveals hidden nodes on demand.

conops.paraphrase: When a visitor activates the '+N more' affordance, all previously hidden low-connectivity nodes render as pills within that lane.

requirements.title: The /graph page shall omit the "+N more" affordance from any swim-lane that has no hidden nodes

conops.paraphrase: Lanes with full node visibility omit the affordance entirely, keeping the board clean when there are no hidden nodes.

requirements.title: The /graph page shall truncate a swim-lane pill's title text with an ellipsis when it exceeds approximately 25 characters, surfacing the full title via the pill's tooltip and the side panel

amended.reason: Requirement was inverted: the original 'no truncation ever' approach made pills unreadably large and crowded neighbors. The new requirement truncates at ~25 characters but preserves full text via tooltip and side panel, balancing board readability with lossless information access.

requirements.source: user-stated requirement (pill truncation / empty Raw lane), not present in product-vision.md or concept-of-operations.md

requirements.title: The /graph page shall render each swim-lane as a tinted rounded container carrying its folder/taxonomy heading and a short lane descriptor

vision.paraphrase: Tinted lane containers with descriptors provide visual structure and context for each taxonomy cluster, making the board more legible and intentional.

conops.paraphrase: Each lane renders within a tinted rounded container displaying its folder/taxonomy name and a short descriptor of what that lane holds.

requirements.title: The /graph page shall render a swim-lane pill's title in full, without an ellipsis, when that title is within approximately 25 characters
requirements.source: user-stated requirement (pill truncation / empty Raw lane), not present in product-vision.md or concept-of-operations.md

requirements.title: The /graph page shall exclude a folder/taxonomy value from the "4 largest" lane-selection ranking when every one of its nodes is hidden from the board by default
requirements.source: user-stated requirement (pill truncation / empty Raw lane), not present in product-vision.md or concept-of-operations.md
